errors: Compatibility of the induced structures on A ∩ B implicitly requires A ∩ B to be tame in both A and B. Stability of M_E under finite intersections is not stated explicitly, though it is needed for 'les structures s'induisant mutuellement' to make sense. The next page's 'stable par intersections finies' for locally tame parts suggests he was aware of this.

Morphisms of ind-tame spaces are not yet defined on this page ('Je voudrais ... la notion d'application modérée'). So the Proposition on finite limits and sums is stated before the morphisms are pinned down. That is a gap in this draft, not an error.

The role of the hypothesis R_0 ≠ ∅ for the existence of finite sums is not explained. Presumably sums are constructed by embedding into R^I × {e_1} versus R^I × {e_2} as on the previous page, which needs suitable points available. This is unclear from the page.

ideas.what: Strict ind-tame spaces: a set with a covering, hereditary, finite-union-stable family of tame subsets carrying compatible tame structures
ideas.modern_name: Weakly semialgebraic spaces / locally definable spaces / (strict) ind-definable sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Delfs–Knebusch (Locally semialgebraic spaces, 1985; Knebusch, Weakly semialgebraic spaces, 1989); later Edmundo, Peatfield and others in o-minimal geometry; ind-definable sets in model theory (Hrushovski–Loeser)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5 sketches tame topology axiomatically but, as far as I know, not ind-tame spaces

ideas.what: Axiom M8: R is the filtered union of its tame parts, giving a canonical ind-tame structure on R and R^I
ideas.modern_name: Viewing R^n as an ind-object of bounded definable sets (locally definable structure on R^n)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal / semialgebraic geometry folklore (Delfs–Knebusch, van den Dries)

ideas.what: Category of strict ind-tame spaces has finite limits and (under R_0 ≠ ∅) finite sums, compatible with the forgetful functors
ideas.modern_name: Finite completeness/cocompleteness of the category of locally definable spaces

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently formulated, apparently before Delfs–Knebusch, the notion of a space glued from tame (definable) pieces as a strict ind-object. He did so axiomatically, for an arbitrary tame structure on R, which is close to the later o-minimal 'locally definable spaces'. The axiomatic framework M1–M8 anticipates working over any o-minimal structure, not just semialgebraic geometry.
missed.quote: Ind-structures modérées strictes : ceci est : la donnée d'un ens. E, et un ens. de parties M_E sur E (les parties modérées), stable par réunions finies
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents an unpublished precursor of locally definable / weakly definable spaces within Grothendieck's tame-topology program. Mathematically the notions are now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean early definition of ind-tame spaces, essentially the weakly/locally semialgebraic (definable) spaces of Delfs–Knebusch, given axiomatically. Historically interesting as a precursor, but the mathematics itself is routine and now well developed.
transcription_corrections: The category is written 'Esp_M' (Espaces modérés, consistent with the next page's 'Esp_{M}'), not 'Ens_M'.
Header: '(IV) ind-espaces modérés', with the top-right note '(ou ind-espaces modérés)' / page number 7.
'A ∈ M, B ∈ M_A ⇒ B ∈ M' is the hereditary condition (A is a tame part of E, B a tame part of A).
Left margin bottom reads roughly 'Esp_M pour R ... (sans prétention!)'. The margin note 'M1 : M5' refers to the axioms used for the Proposition.
